steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Molybdenite
form.label: a few hundred grams of rhenium a tonne

steps.text: Rhenium is one of the rarest elements in the Earth's crust. It has no ore of its own: it sits inside molybdenite, the molybdenum mineral, in porphyry copper deposits, at a few hundred grams a tonne of molybdenite.
in: Hidden in molybdenum, which is itself a by-product of copper

steps.title: Ride with copper and molybdenum
steps.text: Copper ore is mined and floated, and the molybdenite is floated off from the copper concentrate. Rhenium is a by-product of a by-product: it comes only from copper mines that recover molybdenum.
steps.india: No copper-molybdenum mine with rhenium recovery.

steps.title: Roast and catch
steps.text: When molybdenite is roasted, rhenium turns into an oxide that boils off with the furnace gas. Only roasters fitted with gas scrubbers catch it: the gas is washed with water, and the rhenium is pulled from the wash by ion exchange.
out: Molybdenum oxide, the roaster's main product

steps.title: Crystallise
steps.text: The rhenium is crystallised as ammonium perrhenate, a white salt and the form in which rhenium is traded. Heating the salt in hydrogen gives rhenium metal powder.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Metal powder is pressed into pellets and melted into nickel superalloys, at 3 to 6% of the alloy, which are cast as single crystals into turbine blades. The salt is loaded with platinum onto alumina pellets as a catalyst.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Rhenium lets turbine blades run hotter without creeping, and hotter engines burn less fuel. Superalloys take about 80% and the platinum-rhenium catalysts that make high-octane petrol about 15%.
steps.india: Aero-engine programmes need it; all of it is imported.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Rhenium is expensive enough that little is wasted. Worn turbine blades and foundry scrap are remelted or chemically stripped, and spent catalysts are returned to the refiner.

sources.title: Takshashila, India Critical Minerals: scores, project records and capability notes (2026)
